description: One cup holds 16 tablespoons. Convert cups to tablespoons and back, with a table for quarter, third, half, and full cups, plus worked examples.

faqs.answer: 8 tablespoons. Half of 16 is 8, so half a cup is 8 level tablespoons.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in half a cup?

faqs.answer: 5 tablespoons and 1 teaspoon. A third of a cup is 5.33 tablespoons, and the 0.33 of a tablespoon is one teaspoon.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in a third of a cup?

faqs.answer: 8 tablespoons. A stick is half a cup, and the wrapper is marked in tablespoons so you can cut what you need.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in a stick of butter?

faqs.answer: No. A US tablespoon is 14.79 ml. A metric tablespoon is 15 ml, close enough to swap. An Australian tablespoon is 20 ml, about a third larger, so check the source of the recipe.
faqs.question: Is a tablespoon the same size everywhere?

faqs.answer: The count is the same, 16 tablespoons to the cup, because both are volume. The method differs: spoon flour into the tablespoon and level it, and pour liquids to the brim.
faqs.question: Do I measure flour and water the same way?

felicityNote: The tablespoon is my backup cup measure. When the cup is in the dishwasher and the recipe says a third of a cup, five tablespoons and a teaspoon gets dinner moving.

howToSteps.name: Read the cups
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in cups in your recipe. A quarter, a third, a half, three quarters, or a whole number of cups are the usual amounts.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 16
howToSteps.text: Cups times 16 gives tablespoons. Half a cup is 8 tablespoons, a full cup is 16, two cups is 32.

howToSteps.name: Split the thirds
howToSteps.text: A third of a cup is 5 tablespoons and 1 teaspoon. Two thirds is 10 tablespoons and 2 teaspoons. The decimal is 5.33 and 10.67, but spoons are easier.

howToSteps.name: Measure level spoons
howToSteps.text: Fill each tablespoon and level it with the back of a knife. Count as you go, and add the total to the bowl.

name: Cups to Tablespoons
title: US Cups to Tablespoons Converter
tutorial: Sixteen tablespoons make a cup. That is the whole conversion, and it is exact, not rounded. A US cup is defined as 8 fluid ounces, a fluid ounce is 2 tablespoons, and 8 times 2 is 16. Every cup measure in every American kitchen is built on that number.

The conversion matters most when the cup measure is dirty, missing, or the wrong size for the job. A recipe that calls for a third of a cup of oil is easier to measure as 5 tablespoons plus a teaspoon than to eyeball in a two-cup jug. Small amounts are more accurate in spoons, because the lines on a jug are too coarse to read a quarter cup with confidence.

Thirds are the one awkward case. A third of a cup is 5.33 tablespoons, which is 5 tablespoons and 1 teaspoon. Two thirds is 10.67 tablespoons, which is 10 tablespoons and 2 teaspoons. Those two spoon counts are worth memorising, because recipes use thirds constantly and the converter will give you the decimal, not the spoon count.

Level spoons, always. A heaped tablespoon of flour can hold half as much again as a level one, and the conversion assumes level. Fill the spoon, then sweep the back of a knife across the top. For liquids, fill to the brim without letting it dome over the edge.

Dry or liquid, the count is the same. Sixteen tablespoons of water and sixteen tablespoons of flour both fill a cup, because a tablespoon measures volume, not weight. What changes is how you fill the spoon: spoon flour in and level it, pour liquids to the brim.
